creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
move: Scopes the project as an upgrade of an already-validated PICO-8 prototype whose earlier video drew requests for more

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: PICO-8's limits block his ambitions (hand-placed platforms, no editor, collision pain)
move: Switches engines to Godot and enrols in a university class to learn it properly before the main build
reveals: Will pay a real learning cost for the right tool instead of contorting the design to a weak one

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Ramping up on the new engine

reveals: Small tight-loop prototypes as training before the main build - CONFIRMS wave-1 small-proven-tools pattern

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Colour-ring UI does not feel right
move: Iterates through multiple UI versions until one feels right

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Bug: switching colours while inside a block leaves the player stuck
move: First tries the old PICO-8 fix (teleport out); when the new engine's collisions defeat repeated fix attempts, converts the stuck state into a bounce-out mechanic
reveals: MAKER-003 EVIDENCE: fix first, honestly and repeatedly; on failure, canonise - the accident became the game's identity (platformer -> speedrunner). Design failures are material to redesign with, not obstacles to hack past

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Recalling where the bounce idea came from
move: Credits popular viewer comments on the first video
reveals: Audience input steers genre-level direction, not just balance tweaks

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Judging and validating the bouncier pivot
move: Plays it himself repeatedly as the first filter, then has classmates play in person and watches their reactions decide the direction
reveals: Self-playtest as first-pass filter; playtesters as a direction-deciding instrument - CONFIRMS wave-1 team-as-design-instrument pattern

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Playtests split: some players dislike the new speed feel
move: Resists broadening appeal; commits to one specific audience (fans of fast demanding platformers), citing his professor's line that designing for everyone designs for no one
reveals: Design conflict resolved by audience segmentation, never by averaging down

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Reworking controls, flow system, and the per-level timer
move: Filters every change by the primary audience's feel; rejects the timer UI as constant negative information and plans a points-only-ever-go-up feedback system instead
reveals: Polish priorities are audience-aligned feel; feedback layers designed for positive reinforcement; a demotivating system is cut, not patched over

creator: Juniper Dev
title: I Accidentally Made A Speedrunning Game
trigger: Reflecting on the process; winter break removes in-person testers
